recipes.name: Easy Pork Chop Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Stir mushroom soup, water, mushrooms, and onion soup mix in a medium bowl until well combined.

Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add pork chops and cook until until browned on both sides, about 3 to 4 minutes per side. Transfer to a 9x9-inch baking dish and cover with mushroom soup mixture.
Bake in the preheated oven for 1 1/2 hours, or until internal pork temperature reaches 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Pork Chop Casserole
raw_recipe.description: Seared pork chops are baked in cream of mushroom soup that has been perked up with onion soup mix and fresh mushrooms. So simple, so delicious!

review.reviewBody: The whole family gave this recipe a thumbs up. I cooked mine in the crock pot so that the pork chops came out nice and tender. Next time I would use half the water called for so that the gravy is a little thicker but we all thought the flavor was great! Thanks Karen.

Wonderful basic recipe to build from! I used a cast iron dutch oven, seared 3-4 diced garlic cloves w/the chops, added ~8 baby potatoes (skin on, halved), and a pint jar of home grown, canned green beans (drained). For the soup sauce, 1/2 can of water + 1/2 can heavy cream, 2 healthy pinches of dried thyme. ~20 mins b4 done, topped w/a thin layer of crunchy garlic pepper onions, shredded mozzarella & provolone cheese. Total yum. 😋 (Maybe my oven or the cast iron, but I cooked at 325F to go the full 1.5 hrs)

I used veg broth instead of water and I used 12 (small) boneless pork chop cutlets to serve 6 people, instead of the 4 chops in the recipe. Served it with warm homemade applesauce. Pork was so tender! Great meal.

After reading the reviews, I used 6 thin, bone in pork chops, 1 can cream of mushroom soup, 8 oz. fresh sliced mushrooms, 1 package lipton onion soup mix, 1/2 soup can of water, 1 cup sour cream, a little dried parsley and about 1 clove of garlic. I did not brown my pork chops becasue I thought they would be overcooked. Worked great! -- We served it over rice and loved it. I'll try it with chicken next time.
This sounded good. I don't usually change the recipe but I did. I added 1/2 cup of uncooked rice and frozen broccoli. It absorbed the sauce and worked and the dish was delicious.
Excellent! Very easy to make too. I added the extra mushrooms, cut down on the water to thicken the gravy and my pork chops were done after 45 minutes. Definitely will make this again.

I have been making this dish for years! My mother made it often but here are our tweaks: Using about 5-6 boneless chops, brown and set aside. Saute some mushrooms and add the mushroom soup, 1/2 can of beer (any kind) and 2 T. of the dry onion soup mix--stir together well. Add the browned chops and simmer for about 20 minutes. It takes about 10 min. of prep work. 

It's not exactly healthy but it's delicious and husband loves it! The gravy is great over brown rice.

Chops are now in the crock pot so, I won't know exactly how they turn out for a while. But.........I had to alter the recipe as to the amount I needed. I used 6 very thickly cut chops, put a few slivers of garlic inside each one. I also used a family size can of cream of mushroom soup, a tad bit of Worcestershire Sauce, an entire package of dry onion soup mix, fresh mushroom slices and enough water for a nice gravy consistency. Also of course browned the chops as directed. I tasted the gravy mixture before adding to the chops, not too salty because I had basically double of everything. Tasted wonderful not even in the crock pot yet! Am anxious to see how these turn out.....will update. You really could serve these with noodles or potatoes, it's a versatile recipe. I don't see why you couldn't add sliced potatoes and onions if so desired. I think I'll go with buttered egg noodles tonight and a nice salad. Thanks for this (assumingly) great recipe! It seems like a wonderful starter recipe!

I’ve made this recipe for years and have made adjustments along the way. Here’s my version: omit can of water and dry onion soup mix. Instead, add one can of concentrated French onion soup. Stir into the cream of mushroom soup.

I've been making a version of this recipe for years. I omit the dry onion soup, way to salty, and use the cream of mushroom soup and fresh mushrooms (8oz.) size but I slice and fry them before adding them to the soup. I also add 1 T. of Soy Sauce to the soup and mushrooms before baking for 1 hr.

Wow! This was delicious!! I added extra mushrooms and chopped onion, seasoned the chops with salt and pepper before browning, and baked for 30 min. covered, then 15 min. uncovered. Incredibly easy and delicious! I will definitely be making this again!
Great recipe. So easy to make! I used a cast iron skillet and drained the oil off before adding the soup mixture and baking it in the same skillet. Less pans to clean.
Wouldn’t make this again, not much flavor

This is easy and delicious- definitely a keeper! Based on the reviews, I decided to do half the can of water and half heavy cream for a thicker sauce, which worked out well. My pork was also done nicely after 45 minutes.
Cook only 40 minutes!!!! Excellent taste and super easy!
Awesome and simple. Added another can of mushroom soup.
Fast, easy, good! Added cooked rice under the chops which nicely soaked up the sauce.
very watery but the pork chops were tender and juicy. I only had to cook it for 25min
